title: AI Policy
description: The policy a project declares to select which AI standards apply to it and at what level. Nothing in this file asserts compliance; what a project actually meets comes from a validation run. Note the filename: AIStandards reads ai-policy.yml, not project-policy.yml, because EngineeringStandards' policy schema is closed and pins its own standardVersion, so one file cannot satisfy both packs.

standardVersion.description: The AIStandards framework version this policy is written against. A verdict is refused when this disagrees with the framework's VERSION, because a verdict that misstates which rules produced it is a false green.

project.description: The project this policy governs. Reported in the verdict so a consumer can see which repository was evaluated.

rules.description: Every rule the project adopts, and at what level. A rule omitted here is not off — it is undeclared, and the verdict reports how many were left undeclared.

applicability.description: Rules whose SUBJECT does not exist in this project. This is a claim about the project, not about the rule, and it stops being true the moment the project gains the capability — which is what revisitWhen is for. Not-applicable and exception are different mechanisms and never substitute for each other.

ruleId.description: Canonical rule identity: category.kebab-case-name. camelCase spellings are rejected by construction.

reason.description: Why the rule's subject does not exist here. An entry without one is indistinguishable from a rule somebody forgot.

revisitWhen.description: The change that would make this declaration false.
